headline: TikTok's chief executive said AI could deliver real scientific breakthroughs in physics, biotechnology, chemistry and materials within two to three years.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: the News International's text supports the headline, but it is a forecast by a company chief with no named result or date.
importance_line: A prediction that AI will speed up science bears on researchers and on patients who would gain from faster discoveries, then on AI labs including ByteDance, which is building such models itself; it is an executive's forecast, not a result, and he named no specific discovery.
summary: The News International reports that Shou Zi Chew, chief executive of TikTok, told the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference in Singapore on Monday 12 Oct that "in the next two to three years" AI will bring "a real scientific breakthrough" in physics, biotech, chemistry and materials science, which he called "very, very, very possible", adding that the question then would be "how do you align the models?", meaning how to keep them working to human goals. He said ByteDance, TikTok's parent company, is building its own models to speed research and wants to work with scientists, and the outlet notes that ByteDance's Seed research team launched Protenix-v2, an AI model that predicts and designs biomolecular structures for drug discovery, in April.
notes: CNBC's page (the pool item) is blocked (403); the url is The News International page where the remarks were read, and the source is that outlet, which wrote its own account and does not cite CNBC. Same DBS conference as C05-04, C05-05 and C05-06.
